findings.F1: When a coin is in the bottom fifth of its 7-day return scaled by its 60-day volatility, its next 2-day excess return falls as its signed 1-day move rises: slope −0.0100 per unit of z, t −8.98, n 3004 non-overlapping cases; at 3 days the slope is −0.0127, t −8.84, n 2005; the middle and top fifths have flat or positive slopes (+0.0003 t 0.25, +0.0068 t 3.01, +0.0022 t 1.81, +0.0013 t 1.13).
findings.F2: Split by the sign of the prior 7-day return, the 1-day move's sign reverses in falling coins and persists in rising ones: down-trend slope −0.0040 (t −4.11, n 7580) against up-trend slope +0.0025 (t 3.19, n 7440), and −0.0063 (t −5.61) against +0.0049 (t 4.24) at 3 days.
findings.F3: In falling coins, days down by more than one usual move are followed by +0.0080 excess over 2 days (t 3.11, n 923), while up days of 0.3 to 1 usual moves are followed by −0.0070 (t −4.41, n 1755); in rising coins, up days of more than one usual move are followed by +0.0093 (t 3.40, n 1056).
findings.F4: The 1-day move's z times the prior 7-day z predicts the next 2-day excess return with slope +0.0021 (t 4.74, n 15020), but the signed z alone predicts nothing (slope −0.0007, t −1.18).
findings.F5: The move-against-the-7-day-trend measure keeps its effect when the tested idea's absolute move size is in the same regression (t −4.86 against absz t 2.58), so the tested idea misses most of the pattern.
findings.F6: The against-trend slope is negative in 15 of 19 coins and in 7 of 8 years, with t at or below −2.7 in 2021, 2023, 2024 and 2025; 2020 goes the other way (t +3.87), and so do the down-trend reversals in that year (t +2.16).
findings.F7: The book does not lead the coins on any weekday: on Saturday the book averages +0.00053 a day against the coins' +0.0043, and on Wednesday +0.0018 against +0.0043; the weekday split of large moves showed no cell that stands out from the many tested (Sunday large up moves −0.0266, t −2.55, n 106 is the extreme).

ideas.idea: When a coin's 7-day return is negative, the further its latest 1-day move falls relative to its 60-day volatility, the more the coin rises over the next 2 days. The effect is stronger the deeper the coin's 7-day fall relative to its volatility.
ideas.consequence: In a falling coin, a sharp down day is a reason to lean long and a strong up day is a reason to lean short for the next two to three days.
ideas.name: downtrend daily moves reverse

ideas.idea: The more a coin's latest 1-day move, relative to its 60-day volatility, points the same way as its 7-day return, relative to its volatility, the more the coin rises over the next 2 days.
ideas.consequence: A day that extends the coin's weekly direction, down into a fall or up into a rise, is a reason to lean long for the next two days, more so the stronger both are.
ideas.name: trend-aligned move then rise

ideas.idea: When a coin's 7-day return is positive, the larger its latest 1-day rise relative to its 60-day volatility, the more the coin rises over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: In a rising coin, a strong up day is a reason to stay or lean long for the next few days, not to fade it.
ideas.name: uptrend strong days continue
